transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Ever since the car crash, it’s like the accident keeps replaying in my head when I’m awake and when I’m trying to relax, and I can’t shut it off. It just feels like I'm constantly stuck in that moment and I can't get any peace.
How long ago was the car crash, and have these replaying memories and feeling stuck been going on for more than a month?

The car crash happened about four and a half months ago. All of this—the replaying memories and feeling constantly on edge—started a few weeks after the accident and has been going on consistently for about four months now.
Since the crash, have you been avoiding reminders of it, like driving, certain roads, conversations, or thoughts about what happened? If so, what kinds of things do you avoid?

Yeah, I do everything I can to avoid those reminders. I make excuses to my parents and friends so I don't have to get in a car, and I won't go anywhere near that intersection where it happened. If anyone even starts talking about the crash, I just shut down or change the subject because I feel like I'll completely lose it if I let myself think about it.
Since the crash, have you noticed lasting changes in how you think or feel, like blaming yourself or others, feeling detached from people, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah, I keep thinking that if I'd done something differently that morning, my friend wouldn't have been hurt, which makes me feel like a total screw-up. I'm stuck with this constant mix of guilt and tension, and I've even started bailing on my church group and friends because I just can't handle being around people anymore.
Since the crash, have you been more jumpy or easily startled, irritable, or had trouble sleeping or concentrating? Which of those has been happening to you?

Honestly, I've been dealing with almost all of those. I barely sleep because I stare at the ceiling for hours and wake up from half-dreams of screeching brakes, and I'm so irritable that I keep snapping at my little brother and callers at work. I also feel constantly on edge and zone out a lot, which makes it really hard to concentrate on my job.
